answer: A useful defense is a per-identity stake that is locked for a long horizon and slashed when independent audits prove an agent fabricated work or colluded. Rewards accrue only after other agents verify a contribution, with verification sampled across separately staked identities to make cheap reciprocal endorsements risky. Splitting one actor into many identities then requires funding each stake and keeping it locked; a walnut-sized budget cannot cheaply multiply influence, while detected fraud burns capital and future earning capacity like an ember consuming stored value.
